from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Curl: The Rotation Measure", [
            "Curl measures rotation around a point.",
            "Think of a small spinning pinwheel.",
            "Circulation is non-zero in swirling fields."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # Particles rotating (visualizing curl) with pinwheel asset
        center = self.grid['C4']
        pinwheel = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pinwheel.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(pinwheel, 'C4', scale_factor=0.5)
        pinwheel.set_color("#00FF00")
        self.add(pinwheel)
        
        particles = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.05).move_to(center + rotate_vector(RIGHT * 1.5, angle)) for angle in np.linspace(0, 2*PI, 12, endpoint=False)])
        self.add(particles)
        
        def update_particles(mob, dt):
            mob.rotate(dt * 0.5, about_point=center)
            pinwheel.rotate(dt * 0.5)
        particles.add_updater(update_particles)
        self.wait(2)
        particles.remove_updater(update_particles)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Using pinwheel already placed
        self.play(Rotate(pinwheel, angle=2*PI, run_time=2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        arc = Arc(start_angle=0, angle=1.5*PI, radius=0.8, color=WHITE, arc_center=center)
        arrow = Arrow(arc.get_start(), arc.get_end(), buff=0, color=WHITE).scale(0.3)
        self.play(Create(arc), Create(arrow))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-world Application", [
            "Divergence is expansion; curl is rotation.",
            "Essential for understanding fluid dynamics.",
            "Crucial for engineering and meteorology."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Representing divergence and curl with simple vector fields
        field_div = ArrowVectorField(lambda pos: pos, x_range=[-1, 1, 0.5], y_range=[-1, 1, 0.5], colors=[BLUE]).scale(0.5)
        field_curl = ArrowVectorField(lambda pos: np.array([-pos[1], pos[0], 0]), x_range=[-1, 1, 0.5], y_range=[-1, 1, 0.5], colors=[RED]).scale(0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(field_div, "B3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(field_curl, "B4", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(field_div), FadeIn(field_curl))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Representing fluid dynamics with Asset
        fluid_stream = StreamLines(lambda p: np.array([1, np.sin(p[0]), 0]), stroke_width=2, max_anchors_per_line=5).scale(0.6)
        turbine = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/turbine.svg", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_in_area(fluid_stream, "D4", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(turbine, "E3", scale_factor=0.3)
        
        self.play(Create(fluid_stream), FadeIn(turbine))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        apps_text = Text("Applications", color="#FFFF00", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(apps_text, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(apps_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Divergence and Curl: Understanding Vector Fields

sections.title: Introduction: The Concept of a Vector Field
sections.content: Define a vector field as a function that assigns a vector to every point in space (e.g., wind velocity). Briefly introduce the 'fluid flow' metaphor as a foundation for understanding movement and change.
sections.example: Visualize a school of fish swimming; each fish represents a vector showing the speed and direction of the current at that specific point.

sections.title: Divergence: Source vs. Sink
sections.content: Explain divergence (div F) as a scalar measure of 'spreading out' or 'compressing' at a point. Use the ∇ operator dot product: ∇ · F. Emphasize: Positive divergence = source, Negative divergence = sink.
sections.example: Imagine a sprinkler head (source) pushing water out in all directions vs. a vacuum cleaner nozzle (sink) pulling air inward.

sections.title: Curl: The Rotation Measure
sections.content: Explain curl (∇ × F) as a vector measure of rotation around a point. If you place a tiny 'pinwheel' in the field, curl tells you how fast and in what axis it spins.
sections.example: Visualize a whirlpool in a bathtub. Even if the water is moving fast, if it moves in a straight line, the curl is zero; if it swirls, the curl is non-zero.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis: Divergence vs. Curl
sections.content: Side-by-side graphical comparison. Show a divergent field (expanding rays) vs. a curl field (tangential circles) using heat maps to represent magnitude.
sections.example: A spinning fan blade: the air near the center has high curl, while the air pushed forward by the blade blades exhibits divergence.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Quick recap: Divergence measures expansion; Curl measures circulation. Link to Maxwell's equations or fluid dynamics to show why these concepts are essential in engineering.
sections.example: How meteorologists use divergence and curl data from satellites to predict the development and rotation of hurricanes.
